reason: The checker must answer: is this boolean-context operand typed Promise (or a configured promise class), with no union including a falsy type? The port flags only `new Promise(...)` or `x.then(...)` in conditions or as operands of !, &&, || and ?:, with 100% precision and 6% recall. Checker APIs: getTypeAtLocation + union parts + symbol name (:141-152). Line 10 needs the return type of an `async` function, line 18 a declared union, custom-promise line 9 an initializer's class.

evidence.why: `!!promiseFunc()` is flagged only because promiseFunc is `async`. Line 8 `"text" + promiseFunc()` shows the call itself is not the signal
`promiseOrUndefined || ...` is Promise<any> | undefined, so it is not flagged. Only the declared union type distinguishes it
`if (customPromise)`: the variable's class comes from its initializer, and the promise class comes from rule options
